differences.title: 1. SCALABILITY
differences.leftDesc: Automatically scales based on demand, no infrastructure management needed.
differences.rightDesc: Scales by adding/removing container instances, requires some configuration.

differences.title: 2. COST MODEL
differences.leftDesc: Only pay for compute time consumed by your code execution.
differences.rightDesc: Pay for allocated resources (CPU, RAM) even when idle.

differences.title: 3. VENDOR LOCK-IN
differences.leftDesc: Tied to specific cloud provider's FaaS offerings and APIs.
differences.rightDesc: More portable across different cloud providers and on-premise.

differences.title: 4. COLD STARTS
differences.leftDesc: Can experience latency on first invocation after a period of inactivity.
differences.rightDesc: Containers are typically kept warm, ready to serve requests.

differences.title: 5. STATE MANAGEMENT
differences.leftDesc: Functions are designed to be short-lived and stateless.
differences.rightDesc: Containers can maintain application state between requests.

differences.title: 6. DEPLOYMENT UNIT
differences.leftDesc: Deploy and manage code at the function level.
differences.rightDesc: Package and deploy the entire application or service as a unit.

differences.title: 7. COMPLEXITY
differences.leftDesc: Ideal for event-driven tasks and microservices with simple logic.
differences.rightDesc: Offers greater control over environment and dependencies for complex apps.
